10 Easy Ways to Make Your Old Laptop Run Faster in 2026

AC
Alex Chen
November 4, 2026 · 16 min read · 150 views
💻

Is your old laptop getting slower every day? Does it take forever to start, freeze while opening multiple applications, or struggle when you browse the internet? You're not alone. Many laptop users experience these problems as their devices get older.

The good news is that you don't necessarily need to spend hundreds of dollars on a new laptop in 2026. With a few simple adjustments, software improvements, and hardware upgrades, you can make your old laptop feel significantly faster.

Whether you're using an older Windows laptop, a budget laptop, or a device that has been running for five or six years, there are several ways to improve its performance without spending too much money.

In this guide, we'll explore 10 easy and practical ways to make your old laptop run faster in 2026, including beginner-friendly tips that anyone can follow.

Quick answer

To make an old laptop faster, disable startup apps, uninstall unused programs, clean temporary files, reduce background activity, scan for malware, improve cooling, and upgrade from an HDD to an SSD. If your laptop supports it, adding more RAM can also improve multitasking.

Why Is Your Old Laptop Running So Slowly?

Before fixing your laptop, it's important to understand why it has become slow.

Over time, laptops collect unnecessary files, background applications, temporary data, and outdated software. These things can consume valuable system resources and affect overall performance.

Here are some common reasons why an old laptop becomes slow:

  • Too many applications running in the background.
  • Limited RAM (Random Access Memory).
  • Traditional HDD instead of a faster SSD.
  • Low available storage space.
  • Too many startup applications.
  • Outdated operating system and drivers.
  • Malware, unwanted programs, or browser extensions.
  • Overheating caused by dust and poor ventilation.
  • Aging hardware that struggles with modern applications.

The good news is that many of these problems can be fixed with simple maintenance.

1. Disable Unnecessary Startup Programs

One of the easiest ways to speed up an old laptop is to disable unnecessary startup programs.

Have you noticed that your laptop takes several minutes to become usable after pressing the power button? One possible reason is that too many applications automatically launch when Windows starts.

Applications such as messaging tools, cloud storage services, gaming launchers, and update utilities may run automatically in the background.

How to disable startup programs in Windows 11

  1. Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager.
  2. Click on the Startup apps section.
  3. Review the applications listed there.
  4. Identify programs you don't need immediately after startup.
  5. Right-click the unnecessary application.
  6. Select Disable.

You can also access startup settings through Settings → Apps → Startup.

You can usually disable unnecessary music launchers, gaming platforms, and nonessential messaging applications. However, avoid disabling security software, essential audio or touchpad utilities, and other important system services unless you know what they do.

Pro Tip: Don't disable everything. Keep applications that you genuinely need running in the background.

2. Uninstall Unnecessary Applications and Programs

Over the years, most laptop users install dozens of applications that they eventually stop using.

Some programs are installed for a specific task and never opened again. Others come preinstalled by the manufacturer.

These unnecessary applications can consume storage space, run background processes, and sometimes slow down your system.

How to uninstall unwanted applications

  1. Open Windows Settings.
  2. Select Apps.
  3. Click Installed apps.
  4. Review the installed programs.
  5. Find applications you no longer need.
  6. Click the three-dot menu beside the application.
  7. Select Uninstall and follow the instructions.

Consider uninstalling old games, unused editing software, duplicate applications, unnecessary manufacturer utilities, trial software, and applications you installed but never use.

Be careful not to remove important drivers, Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributables, security applications, or programs you don't recognize without checking their purpose.

3. Upgrade Your Old Hard Drive to an SSD

If your laptop still uses a traditional HDD (Hard Disk Drive), upgrading to an SSD (Solid State Drive) can make one of the biggest differences in everyday performance.

An HDD stores data on spinning magnetic disks, while an SSD uses flash memory. SSDs can access data much faster because they don't depend on moving mechanical components.

An SSD can improve:

  • Windows startup time.
  • Application loading speed.
  • File transfer performance.
  • System responsiveness.
  • Overall everyday usability.

How to upgrade your laptop to an SSD

  1. Check whether your laptop supports a SATA SSD or an M.2 SSD.
  2. Check the manufacturer's specifications for compatible storage.
  3. Choose an SSD with sufficient capacity.
  4. Back up your important files.
  5. Clone your existing drive or perform a fresh operating system installation.
  6. Install the SSD following your laptop manufacturer's instructions.

If you're unfamiliar with laptop hardware, consider getting help from a technician.

An SSD upgrade is often worth it in 2026, especially if your laptop currently uses an HDD. However, remember that an SSD improves storage performance rather than turning an old processor into a modern one.

4. Increase Your Laptop's RAM

RAM plays an important role in laptop performance.

RAM stands for Random Access Memory. It temporarily stores information that your computer needs while running applications.

When your laptop doesn't have enough RAM, Windows may use your storage drive as virtual memory. This can make the system feel slow, especially when multiple applications are open.

How much RAM do you need in 2026?

RAM Recommended usage
4GBVery basic tasks; often limiting
8GBBasic browsing and office work
16GBComfortable everyday multitasking
32GBHeavy multitasking and demanding workloads

Before buying additional memory, check your laptop's maximum RAM capacity, whether RAM is upgradeable or soldered, compatible DDR generation, supported memory speed, and the number of available memory slots.

5. Clean Temporary Files and Free Up Storage Space

Another common reason for slow laptop performance is a nearly full storage drive.

When your system drive has very little free space, Windows may have less room for temporary files, updates, caching, and virtual memory management.

How to remove temporary files in Windows 11

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Go to System.
  3. Select Storage.
  4. Click Temporary files.
  5. Review the categories.
  6. Select the files you want to remove.
  7. Click Remove files.

You can also enable Storage Sense to automatically remove certain unnecessary files.

As a practical target, try to maintain around 15–20% free space when possible. This is particularly useful on laptops with smaller SSDs.

6. Turn Off Unnecessary Background Applications

Sometimes your laptop feels slow even when you're not actively using many applications.

That may happen because some programs continue running in the background.

Cloud synchronization tools, update utilities, messaging applications, and other services may consume CPU, RAM, network bandwidth, and battery power.

How to identify resource-consuming applications

  1. Open Task Manager using Ctrl + Shift + Esc.
  2. Select the Processes tab.
  3. Check the CPU, Memory, and Disk columns.
  4. Identify applications using unusually high resources.
  5. Close applications you don't currently need.

Avoid ending unfamiliar Windows system processes. Some background processes are necessary for Windows to operate correctly.

7. Update Windows, Drivers, and Essential Software

Keeping your laptop updated is another important step toward maintaining good performance.

Software updates often include bug fixes, security improvements, compatibility updates, and performance optimizations.

How to update Windows

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Select Windows Update.
  3. Click Check for updates.
  4. Install available updates.
  5. Restart your laptop if required.

How to update device drivers

  1. Right-click the Start button.
  2. Open Device Manager.
  3. Expand the hardware category you want to check.
  4. Right-click the device.
  5. Select Update driver.

You can also download compatible drivers directly from your laptop manufacturer's official support website.

Important: Windows 10 reached the end of its standard support lifecycle on October 14, 2025. If you're still using it, check your eligibility for Windows 11 or available Extended Security Updates.

8. Scan Your Laptop for Viruses and Malware

Malware is another possible reason why your old laptop is running slowly.

Some unwanted programs consume system resources in the background. Others may display unwanted advertisements, redirect browser searches, or interfere with normal system operations.

How to scan your laptop using Windows Security

  1. Open the Start menu.
  2. Search for Windows Security.
  3. Select Virus & threat protection.
  4. Click Quick scan.
  5. Follow the recommended security actions.

If you suspect a more serious infection, consider running a Full scan or Microsoft Defender Offline scan.

Malware removal can improve performance if unwanted software is consuming CPU, RAM, or storage resources. However, malware is not always the reason for a slow computer.

9. Prevent Overheating by Cleaning Your Laptop

Have you noticed that your laptop becomes extremely hot when browsing the internet, watching videos, or running applications?

Overheating can significantly affect laptop performance.

Modern processors automatically reduce their operating speed when temperatures become too high. This process is known as thermal throttling.

How to prevent laptop overheating

  1. Keep your laptop on a hard, flat surface.
  2. Avoid using it on beds, blankets, or pillows.
  3. Keep air vents clear.
  4. Clean external vents regularly.
  5. Check whether the cooling fan is working properly.
  6. Have the internal fan and heatsink cleaned when necessary.

If you are comfortable opening your laptop, you may clean the cooling system using appropriate tools and manufacturer-approved procedures. Otherwise, let a qualified technician handle internal cleaning.

Thermal paste may also deteriorate over time. Replacing it can help some older laptops, but it should be done carefully because improper installation can cause hardware damage.

10. Adjust Windows Visual Effects for Better Performance

Windows includes several visual effects designed to make the operating system look attractive.

Animations, shadows, transparency, and other graphical effects can consume some system resources.

On modern computers, these effects usually have little impact. However, on older laptops with limited hardware, reducing unnecessary visual effects can make the interface feel more responsive.

How to adjust visual effects in Windows 11

  1. Press Windows + R.
  2. Type sysdm.cpl.
  3. Press Enter.
  4. Open the Advanced tab.
  5. Under Performance, click Settings.
  6. Select Adjust for best performance.
  7. Click Apply.

Alternatively, select Custom and keep the effects you prefer. For example, you can retain smooth font edges while disabling unnecessary animations and shadows.

Bonus Tips: Extra Ways to Improve Your Old Laptop's Performance

The ten methods above cover the most important improvements. However, here are a few additional tips that can help you maintain your laptop in 2026.

  • Use fewer browser tabs: Opening too many browser tabs can consume substantial RAM. Close tabs you don't need and remove unnecessary extensions.
  • Choose the appropriate power mode: Go to Settings → System → Power & battery and choose Best performance when plugged in, if available.
  • Move large files to external storage: Store old videos, photos, and documents on an external drive to free up internal storage.
  • Restart your laptop regularly: Restarting can clear temporary system states and resolve certain performance issues caused by long-running processes.

Which Upgrade Makes the Biggest Difference?

Not every laptop needs the same improvement. The best solution depends on the hardware currently installed.

Laptop problem Recommended solution
Very slow startupSSD upgrade, startup cleanup
Slow multitaskingRAM upgrade
Almost full storageRemove unnecessary files
Laptop freezes frequentlyCheck RAM, storage, and malware
Laptop gets very hotClean cooling system
Slow application loadingSSD upgrade
Slow browsingReduce tabs and extensions
Slow Windows interfaceReduce visual effects

My recommendation: If your laptop still has a traditional HDD, consider an SSD upgrade first. If it already has an SSD but struggles with multiple applications, check whether additional RAM is supported.

Should You Upgrade Your Old Laptop or Buy a New One?

This is an important question for anyone using an older laptop.

Sometimes a few inexpensive upgrades are enough to make an old laptop useful for several more years. In other cases, replacing the device is the more practical choice.

Consider upgrading your old laptop if:

  • It has a reasonably capable processor.
  • It supports an SSD upgrade.
  • Its RAM can be increased.
  • Its battery and display are still in good condition.
  • You mainly use it for browsing, office work, online classes, and basic productivity.

Consider buying a new laptop if:

  • Its processor is extremely outdated.
  • It doesn't support your required operating system.
  • The motherboard or other major components are failing.
  • It cannot run the applications you need.
  • Repair and upgrade costs are close to the price of a suitable replacement.

Remember that performance improvements depend on your laptop's hardware limitations. An SSD and more RAM can help significantly, but they cannot solve every limitation of an aging processor.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. How can I make my old laptop faster without spending money?

You can improve performance without spending money by disabling unnecessary startup applications, uninstalling unused programs, removing temporary files, closing background applications, scanning for malware, and reducing unnecessary visual effects.

These changes can make a noticeable difference, particularly if your laptop is slowed down by software rather than hardware.

2. Does upgrading RAM make an old laptop faster?

Yes, upgrading RAM can improve performance when your laptop frequently runs out of available memory.

For example, increasing RAM from 4GB to 8GB or 16GB may improve multitasking, depending on hardware compatibility and workload. However, if your laptop already has sufficient RAM, adding more may not provide a noticeable improvement.

3. Is an SSD better than an HDD for an old laptop?

Yes. SSDs generally provide much faster storage performance than traditional HDDs.

An SSD can improve boot times, application loading, and general system responsiveness. It is often one of the most worthwhile upgrades for older laptops.

4. Why is my laptop slow even after cleaning it?

Cleaning unnecessary files doesn't fix every performance problem.

Your laptop may still be slow because of insufficient RAM, an aging processor, overheating, failing storage, malware, or incompatible software. Check Task Manager to identify whether CPU, memory, or disk usage is unusually high.

5. Can I make my old laptop run faster without reinstalling Windows?

Yes. You can disable startup applications, uninstall unwanted programs, upgrade hardware, clean temporary files, update drivers, and optimize visual effects without reinstalling Windows.

A fresh Windows installation can sometimes help with persistent software problems, but it isn't necessary as a first step.

6. Does factory resetting a laptop make it faster?

A factory reset can improve performance if your laptop has accumulated unnecessary applications, corrupted settings, or problematic software.

However, it won't improve hardware limitations such as insufficient RAM or an outdated processor. Always back up important files before resetting your laptop.

7. How much RAM is enough for an old laptop in 2026?

For basic everyday use, 8GB is a reasonable starting point. For smoother multitasking, 16GB is generally more comfortable.

Your actual requirements depend on the operating system, browser, and applications you use.

8. Can an old laptop run Windows 11 smoothly?

Some older laptops can run Windows 11 smoothly, provided they meet the official hardware requirements.

However, compatibility alone doesn't guarantee good performance. Processor capability, RAM, storage type, and cooling also matter. Check Microsoft's official Windows 11 system requirements before upgrading.

Final Thoughts: Give Your Old Laptop a Second Life in 2026

You don't always need a brand-new laptop to enjoy better computer performance.

Sometimes, simple maintenance and a few smart upgrades are all you need to make your existing device faster and more reliable.

Start by disabling unnecessary startup applications, removing unused programs, cleaning temporary files, and reducing background activity. These improvements are free and easy to perform.

If your laptop still feels slow, consider upgrading its HDD to an SSD or increasing its RAM, provided your hardware supports those upgrades.

Also, don't forget about regular maintenance. Keeping your laptop cool, updated, and free from unnecessary software can help it perform better for longer.

The most important thing to remember is this: Before spending money on a new laptop, find out what's actually making your old one slow. With the right improvements, your old laptop may still be perfectly capable of handling everyday tasks in 2026.
